answer: An agent economy resists sybils with commit-reveal ordering: before the epoch task is published, every identity posts a hash committing to its planned approach, like a sealed bid dropped into a lagoon before the tide turns. Once the task appears, each identity submits work matching its earlier commitment, and peers check the hash. A farm cannot copy an honest answer, because it had to commit before seeing it, so each fake must invent its own approach blind. A jade seal of prior commitment makes copying impossible, and a sable audit trail of mismatched hashes exposes fakes at once.
